claim: Under 15 CFR 400.1(c), activated zones are treated as outside the customs territory of the United States for tariff and entry purposes specified in the Foreign-Trade Zones Act.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: Activated zones are treated as "outside the customs territory of the United States" for tariff and entry purposes, only for purposes specified in the Act.

claim: Duties on foreign goods in a zone generally apply only when the goods enter customs territory for domestic consumption.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: Duties generally apply only once foreign goods "enters customs territory for domestic consumption."

claim: When goods leave a zone for domestic consumption, the importer ordinarily may choose to pay duty at the rate for the foreign material as admitted or, if used in production activity, at the rate for the emerging product.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "ordinarily has a choice of paying duties either at the rate applicable to the foreign material" or the emerging product rate

claim: Production activity in a zone may not be conducted without prior authorization from the Foreign-Trade Zones Board.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "Production activity in zones shall not be conducted without prior authorization from the Board"

claim: The Foreign-Trade Zones Board consists of the Secretary of Commerce, as chairman, and the Secretary of the Treasury.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "consists of the Secretary of the Department of Commerce (chairman) and the Secretary of the Treasury"

claim: 15 CFR 400.2 defines production as activity involving the substantial transformation of a foreign article resulting in a new and different article, or activity changing the article's condition so that its customs classification or eligibility for entry for consumption changes.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "substantial transformation of a foreign article resulting in a new and different article" ... "or activity involving a change in the condition of the article"
verifier_note: Corrected by verifier-V8: § 400.2(o) has a second limb (change in condition affecting classification or entry eligibility); claim and page sentence completed, then verified.

claim: Merchandise moved into a zone for export in zone-restricted status may be considered exported for purposes such as federal excise tax rebates and customs drawback.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: may be considered exported for purposes such as "federal excise tax rebates and customs drawback."
verifier_note: Corrected by verifier-V8: § 400.1(c) applies export treatment to merchandise moved into zones for export under zone-restricted status; qualifier added to claim and sentence, then verified.

claim: Items subject to antidumping or countervailing duty orders must be placed in privileged foreign status when admitted to a zone or subzone.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "shall be placed in privileged foreign status" when admitted "to a zone or subzone."
verifier_note: Text is in 15 CFR 400.13(c)(2) (fetched on the Part 400 page).

claim: 19 CFR 146.1 defines customs territory as the territory of the U.S. in which the general tariff laws of the U.S. apply.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "Customs territory is the territory of the U.S. in which the general tariff laws of the U.S. apply."

claim: An operator is a corporation, partnership, or person that operates a zone or subzone under an agreement with the zone grantee, and a user is a person or firm using a zone for storage, handling, or processing.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "a corporation, partnership, or person that operates a zone or subzone" ... User: using a zone or subzone for storage, handling, or processing

claim: Activation is approval by the grantee and port director for zone operations and for admitting and handling merchandise in zone status.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "Activation" is defined as approval by the grantee and port director for operations and for admitting and handling merchandise in zone status.

claim: Privileged foreign status is given, on application to the port director on Customs Form 214, to foreign merchandise not yet manipulated or manufactured so as to change its tariff classification, and it cannot be abandoned.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "Foreign merchandise which has not been manipulated or manufactured so as to effect a change in tariff classification will be given status"

claim: Privileged foreign merchandise is classified at the rate of duty and tax in force on the date the application for privileged status is filed.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "at the rate of duty and tax in force on the date of filing"

claim: Nonprivileged foreign merchandise is subject to tariff classification in accordance with its character, condition and quantity when it is constructively transferred to customs territory.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "subject to tariff classification in accordance with its character, condition and quantity"

claim: Nonprivileged foreign status covers foreign merchandise in a zone that is neither privileged foreign nor zone-restricted.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 146.42: foreign merchandise in a zone that is neither privileged foreign nor zone-restricted.

claim: Domestic status may be granted to U.S. goods on which applicable internal revenue taxes were paid, previously imported goods on which duty and tax were paid, and previously entered duty-free goods.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 146.43: U.S. goods with internal-revenue taxes paid, previously imported goods with duty and tax paid, or previously entered duty-free goods.

claim: Zone-restricted status applies to merchandise taken into a zone solely for exportation, destruction, or storage; it cannot be abandoned once granted.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: taken into a zone solely for exportation, destruction ... or storage ... "cannot be abandoned once granted."

claim: The port director may allow an entry on Customs Form 3461 for estimated removals during a calendar week of merchandise manufactured or otherwise changed in the zone, excluding packing, within 24 hours before physical transfer.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "for the estimated removals of merchandise during the calendar week" ... "within 24 hours before physical transfer from the zone for consumption."

claim: Privileged foreign merchandise may not be entered for warehouse from a zone.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "may not be entered for warehouse from a zone."

claim: An accepted entry constructively transfers merchandise to customs territory even if it remains physically in the zone.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 146.61: an accepted entry constructively transfers the merchandise to Customs territory, even if it remains physically in the zone.

claim: CBP officers may supervise zone transactions through methods such as periodic audits, inventory counts, or spot checks.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 146.3: supervision through methods such as periodic audits, inventory counts, or spot checks.

claim: Under the alternative site framework, a magnet site is intended to serve multiple operators or users and a usage-driven site is established for a single operator or user.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "intended to serve or attract multiple operators or users under the ASF" ... "established for a single operator or user under the ASF"

claim: A subzone is a site or group of sites established for a specific use.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "a site (or group of sites) established for a specific use"
